hunt.justification: UNC3753 is a high-tempo threat cluster targeting law firms with extortion. Their use of vishing bypasses most automated email/web filters, making endpoint-based behavioral hunting the primary way to detect their presence before data exfiltration occurs.

meta.analysis: A single detection rule would likely fire on any curl command or any RMM tool installation, leading to high false-positive rates. This hunt baselines Privnote usage and RMM presence across the fleet, using an agent to weigh the coincidence of these events on a single host.

stages.name: IT Helpdesk Impersonation and Vishing
observables: Direct phone calls posing as IT support
Screen-sharing session links (Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Quick Assist)

stages.name: VDI Access from Personal Devices
observables: Personal/BYOD IP addresses accessing corporate VDI
Login to corporate VDI after Zoom/Teams sessions

stages.name: Document Search and Staging
observables: Keyword searches for W-2, W-9, 1099, SSN, and audit files
Files staged in native Roaming profile path

stages.name: Exfiltration via Cloud and FTP
observables: Folders renamed to mimic victim branding on cloud storage
Forwarding staged files via internal target mailboxes

scenario.summary: UNC3753 (Silent Ransom Group) uses invoice-themed emails and vishing to trick US law firm employees into installing RMM tools and initiating screen-sharing sessions. The actors pivot from compromised BYOD endpoints to corporate VDI environments, stage sensitive legal and financial documents, and exfiltrate them via cloud storage or FTP for extortion.

meta.rationale: Focus on workstations and endpoints likely to be targeted by vishing (e.g., HR, Finance, Legal). Exclude server infrastructure where RMM tools might be expected.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is using vishing to impersonate IT support and social-engineer users into installing RMM tools via links shared through self-destructing note services.

hunt.name: Vishing-Driven RMM Deployment (UNC3753)
hunt.description: This hunt targets the initial stages of UNC3753 operations, where threat actors use voice phishing (vishing) to bypass technical controls and convince users to install Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) software. The hunt identifies hosts with newly installed RMM packages, identifies suspicious installation commands (like curl downloading MSI files), and correlates these actions with access to self-destructing note services like Privnote, which are used to relay instructions to victims.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, vendor_name FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (instr(',' || '{{rmm_keywords}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(package_name) || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{rmm_keywords}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(vendor_name) || ',') > 0)
config.description: Find hosts where RMM software mentioned in the report is present in the software inventory.
config.expected_signal: Hosts running AnyDesk, SuperOps, or other RMM tools. While many are legitimate, their presence on workstations not typically managed by these specific tools is suspicious.

primitive_config.label: Identify hosts with RMM software
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, vendor_name FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (instr(',' || '{{rmm_keywords}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(package_name) || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{rmm_keywords}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(vendor_name) || ',') > 0)
primitive_config.expected: Hosts running AnyDesk, SuperOps, or other RMM tools. While many are legitimate, their presence on workstations not typically managed by these specific tools is suspicious.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%curl%installer%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%msiexec%/i%quiet%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%superops.msi%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find process command lines indicating an RMM tool being downloaded via curl or installed via msiexec in a quiet mode, as seen in UNC3753 incidents.
config.expected_signal: A curl command downloading an installer or an msiexec command running a newly dropped MSI. This represents the execution phase of the RMM tool.

primitive_config.label: Suspicious RMM installation commands
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%curl%installer%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%msiexec%/i%quiet%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%superops.msi%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A curl command downloading an installer or an msiexec command running a newly dropped MSI. This represents the execution phase of the RMM tool.

config.content: SELECT query_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) as host_count, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE LOWER(query_hostname) = 'privnote.com' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY query_hostname
config.description: Identify hosts resolving privnote.com, which is used by UNC3753 to relay installation commands to victims.
config.expected_signal: A rare resolution of privnote.com on a specific host. In a corporate environment, this service is often used for non-business purposes or shadow IT, but its correlation with RMM installs is highly suspicious.

primitive_config.expected: A rare resolution of privnote.com on a specific host. In a corporate environment, this service is often used for non-business purposes or shadow IT, but its correlation with RMM installs is highly suspicious.

config.objective: Determine if any host shows a combination of rare Privnote access and unauthorized RMM installer execution.
config.description: Correlate the software inventory, suspicious process activity, and DNS traffic to determine if an unauthorized RMM installation occurred via vishing.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious, suspicious, or benign per host, with specific citations for the commands and domains.

config.question: the triage-agent verdict is malicious for any host
config.condition: the triage-agent verdict is malicious for any host

config.instructions: Isolate the host from the network and revoke any active sessions for the affected user. Collect the identified RMM binaries for analysis.
Review the agent's findings. If confirmed, initiate the incident response protocol for data theft. If benign, tune the RMM keyword list to exclude legitimate corporate tools.
